findings.title: totalPages off-by-one creates a phantom empty page
findings.body: totalPages is computed as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 100 members with limit 50, i.e. exactly 2 pages), this yields 3, so showingLast (currentPage == totalPages) is never true on the real last page. The 'next' arrow stays enabled, and clicking it sets offset to min(offset+limit, user_count) = 100, which returns an empty member list while the pager shows '3/3'. Use Math.ceil(user_count / limit) instead.

findings.title: PUT /admin/groups/:id silently flips visible to false for old clients
findings.body: The update action now reads flat params (params[:visible], params[:name], params[:alias_level]) instead of the previous nested params[:group][...] payload, and create likewise changed from params[:group][:name] to params[:name]. Any existing client (admin API script, plugin, or older cached frontend assets still in a user's browser) that PUTs group: {visible: "true", name: ...} will now hit `params[:visible] == "true"` evaluating to false, silently turning group visibility off, while the name and alias_level changes are silently dropped. The parameter format change breaks the published admin API contract with a data-corrupting failure mode rather than a loud error.

findings.title: Unvalidated limit/offset in public members endpoint
findings.body: The members action takes `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` straight from the query string with no upper bound or sign check. The old code capped automatic-group listings at 200; now a single request with limit=100000000 forces the server to load and serialize the entire membership of a group (e.g. trust_level_0 can be every user on the site), an easy amplification/DoS vector on a public, non-admin endpoint. Additionally, negative values (limit=-1 or offset=-1) are passed to ActiveRecord's limit/offset and raise an unhandled error, returning a 500. Clamp limit (e.g. to a few hundred) and reject non-negative offset/limit.

findings.title: Response shape of /groups/:name/members.json changed from array to object
findings.body: The members endpoint previously rendered a bare JSON array of serialized members (`render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)`) and now returns `{members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}}`. This is a public, user-facing endpoint; any consumer other than the in-repo frontend (themes, plugins, external API users parsing the array) will break, since code expecting an array will now iterate the object or read undefined. Even if intentional, this is an unversioned breaking change to a public API that should be called out and, ideally, covered by a controller spec — there are no tests at all for the new pagination/meta format.

findings.title: Stale offset after removing a member leaves admin on an empty page
findings.body: After removeMember succeeds it calls findMembers() with the old offset. The clamp on line 23 uses the client's stale user_count (still pre-removal), so e.g. with 51 members at offset 50, removing the last member re-requests offset 50; the server returns total=50, offset=50 and an empty members array. The UI then shows an empty member list with currentPage=2 and totalPages=1 (so showingLast is false and 'next' keeps firing no-op requests at the same offset). The offset should be re-clamped against the refreshed total (or reset toward the last valid page) when the response comes back.

findings.title: save() error handler crashes when the rejection has no JSON body
findings.body: The failure path does `$.parseJSON(e.responseText).errors` unconditionally. If the promise rejects for anything other than a JSON error response (network failure, timeout, gateway 502 returning HTML, or a rejection value without responseText), `e.responseText` is undefined, $.parseJSON throws, and the user gets no feedback at all (plus a JS error) instead of an alert. It also assumes the payload has an `.errors` key. Guard the parse and fall back to a generic message.

findings.title: remove_member automatic-group test uses PUT instead of DELETE
findings.body: The test 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' calls `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...`, but the route wired up in config/routes.rb is `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`. Because controller specs invoke the action directly, this test passes regardless of whether the DELETE route exists or is correctly constrained — it provides no verification of the actual routing added in this PR. The 'is able to remove a member' test uses :delete correctly, so only the automatic-group guard test is testing the wrong verb.

findings.title: findMembers returns undefined instead of a promise when name is empty
findings.body: The guard clause changed from `return Ember.RSVP.resolve([])` to a bare `return;`. The method's contract was 'returns a promise'; the two current call sites happen not to chain on the result, but any caller doing `group.findMembers().then(...)` (as the previous versions of both routes did via afterModel, and as any plugin or future code would naturally write) will now throw TypeError on undefined. Keep returning a resolved promise for the empty-name case.
